title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 23
paragraphs: As the Samians made their way toward Sicily, they reached Epizephyrian Locri, and at the same time the people of Zancle, both themselves and their king, whose name was Scythes, were encamped around a city of the Sicels, hoping to take it. Perceiving these things, Anaxilaus, tyrant of Rhegium, who was at odds with those of Zancle, communicated with the Samians and persuaded them that they should leave the Fair Strand alone, to which they were sailing, and take possession of Zancle instead, since it was now without men to defend it. The Samians did as he said and took possession of Zancle. The men of Zancle, when they were informed that their city was in enemy hands, set out to rescue it and called on Hippocrates, tyrant of Gela, to help them, for he was their ally. But when Hippocrates too had come up with his army to their rescue, he first put Scythes the ruler of the Zanclaeans in fetters, on the ground that he had been the cause of the city's loss, and together with him his brother Pythogenes, and sent them off to the town of Inyx. He then betrayed the cause of the remaining Zanclaeans by coming to terms with the Samians and exchanging oaths with them; in return for this, it had been promised by the Samians that Hippocrates should receive as his share half of all the movable goods in the city and of the slaves, and the whole of the property in the fields round about. So the greater part of the Zanclaeans he put in bonds and kept as slaves for himself, but the chief men among them, three hundred in number, he handed over to the Samians to put to death—which, however, the Samians did not do.
